topics.title: Surface Areas and Volumes of Basic 3D Shapes
topics.concept:
What is Surface Area and Volume?

  • Surface Area is the total area of all the faces (surfaces) of a three-dimensional object. It is measured in square units (cm², m², etc.).
  • Volume is the amount of space occupied by a three-dimensional object. It is measured in cubic units (cm³, m³, etc.).

Formulas for Basic 3D Shapes:

ShapeLateral/Curved Surface AreaTotal Surface AreaVolume
**Cuboid** (l, b, h)2h(l + b)2(lb + bh + hl)l × b × h
**Sphere** (radius = r)—4πr²(4/3)πr³
**Hemisphere** (radius = r)2πr²3πr²(2/3)πr³
**Right Circular Cylinder** (r, h)2πrh2πr(r + h)πr²h
**Right Circular Cone** (r, h, l)πrlπr(r + l)(1/3)πr²h

Key Terms:

  • l = slant height = √(r² + h²) for a cone
  • Lateral/Curved Surface Area = area of all faces except the base(s)
  • Total Surface Area = lateral surface area + area of base(s)

Formulas for Basic 3D Shapes:

ShapeLateral/Curved Surface AreaTotal Surface AreaVolume
Cube (side = a)4a²6a²a³
Cuboid (l, b, h)2h(l + b)2(lb + bh + hl)l × b × h
Sphere (radius = r)—4πr²(4/3)πr³
Hemisphere (radius = r)2πr²3πr²(2/3)πr³

points: Surface area is measured in square units (cm², m²)
Volume is measured in cubic units (cm³, m³)
Cube: all sides equal; Cuboid: length, breadth, height
Sphere: perfectly round; Hemisphere: half of a sphere
Cylinder: circular base, straight sides; Cone: circular base, pointed top
For cones, slant height l = √(r² + h²)

topics.title: Surface Areas and Volumes of Combined Solids
topics.concept:
What are Combined Solids?

Combined solids are three-dimensional shapes made by joining two or more basic solids. Examples include:

  • A cylinder with a hemisphere on top (like a capsule)
  • A cone mounted on a cylinder (like a tent)
  • A cuboid with a cylindrical hole

How to Find Surface Area of Combined Solids:

  • Add the surface areas of the individual parts
  • Subtract the area of the faces that are joined (they are not exposed)

How to Find Volume of Combined Solids:

  • Simply add the volumes of the individual parts
  • No subtraction needed (volume is additive)

Common Combined Solids:

CombinationShapesApplications
Cone + CylinderCone on top of cylinderTents, ice cream cones
Cuboid + CylinderCuboid with cylindrical holePipes through blocks, bearings
Cone + HemisphereCone on hemisphereRocket nose cones, party hats

sections.content:
What are Combined Solids? Combined solids are three-dimensional shapes made by joining two or more basic solids. Examples include: - A cylinder with a hemisphere on top (like a capsule) - A cone mounted on a cylinder (like a tent) - A cuboid with a cylindrical hole

How to Find Surface Area of Combined Solids: - Add the surface areas of the individual parts - Subtract the area of the faces that are joined (they are not exposed)

How to Find Volume of Combined Solids: - Simply add the volumes of the individual parts - No subtraction needed (volume is additive)

Common Combined Solids:

CombinationShapesApplications
Cylinder + HemisphereCylinder with hemispherical endsCapsules, silos, water tanks
Cone + CylinderCone on top of cylinderTents, ice cream cones
Cuboid + CylinderCuboid with cylindrical holePipes through blocks, bearings
Cone + HemisphereCone on hemisphereRocket nose cones, party hats

COMBINED SOLID - CYLINDER WITH HEMISPHERICAL CAP:

    ┌─────┐
   ╱       ╲
  │         │
  │         │
  │         │
  │ Cylinder│
  │   h     │
  │         │
  │         │
  │         │
  └─────────┘
  
    Hemisphere (radius r)
    Cylinder (radius r, height h)
    
    Total Volume = Volume of cylinder + Volume of hemisphere
                = πr²h + (2/3)πr³
    
    Surface Area = CSA of cylinder + CSA of hemisphere
                = 2πrh + 2πr²


COMBINED SOLID - CONE ON CYLINDER:

          ╱╲
         /  \
        /    \
       /      \
      /        \
     └──────────┘
     │          │
     │ Cylinder │
     │    h₂    │
     │          │
     └──────────┘
     
     Cone (radius r, height h₁)
     Cylinder (radius r, height h₂)
     
     Total Volume = (1/3)πr²h₁ + πr²h₂
     
     TSA = πrl + 2πrh₂ + πr² (base of cylinder)
     (l = slant height of cone = √(r² + h₁²))


COMBINED SOLID - CUBOID WITH CYLINDRICAL HOLE:

    ┌─────────────────────┐
    │                     │
    │    ┌─────────┐     │
    │    │         │     │
    │    │  Hole   │     │
    │    │ (radius │     │
    │    │   r)    │     │
    │    └─────────┘     │
    │                     │
    └────

points: For combined solids, volume adds up directly
Surface area requires subtracting joined faces
Always identify all individual shapes in the combined solid
Draw a diagram to visualize which faces are exposed

topics.title: Conversion of Units
topics.concept:
Why Convert Units?

In real-life problems, measurements may be given in different units. To calculate surface area or volume correctly, all measurements must be in the same unit system.

Length Conversions:

ConversionFormula
m to cmMultiply by 100
mm to cmDivide by 10
cm to mmMultiply by 10
km to mMultiply by 1000
m to kmDivide by 1000

Area Conversions (Square Units):

ConversionFormulaReason
m² to cm²Multiply by 10,000—
mm² to cm²Divide by 1001 cm² = 10 mm × 10 mm = 100 mm²
km² to m²Multiply by 1,000,0001 km² = 1000 m × 1000 m = 1,000,000 m²

Volume Conversions (Cubic Units):

ConversionFormulaReason
m³ to cm³Multiply by 1,000,000—
mm³ to cm³Divide by 10001 cm³ = 10 mm × 10 mm × 10 mm = 1000 mm³
litre (L) to cm³Multiply by 10001 L = 1000 cm³
m³ to litreMultiply by 10001 m³ = 1000 L

FromToMultiply by

m²cm²10,000
cm²m²0.0001
m³cm³1,000,000
cm³m³0.000001

    1 m² = 10,000 cm²
    
    ┌────────────────────────────────────┐
    │                                    │
    │             1 m                     │
    │                                    │
    │                                    │
    │              1 m                   │
    │                                    │
    │                                    │
    └────────────────────────────────────┘
    
    Each small square = 1 cm × 1 cm = 1 cm²
    Total = 100 × 100 = 10,000 small squares = 10,000 cm²
    
    
    VOLUME:
    1 m³ = 1,000,000 cm³
    
    A cube of side 1 m contains:
    100 layers × 100 rows × 100 columns = 1,000,000 small cubes (1 cm³ each)
    
    
    VOLUME AND CAPACITY:
    
    1 L = 1000 mL = 1000 cm³
    
    1 L container:
    ┌─────────┐
    │         │

points: Always convert all measurements to the same unit before calculating
Length conversion: multiply/divide by powers of 10
Area conversion: square the length conversion factor
Volume conversion: cube the length conversion factor

online.title: Online Test — Chapter 13: Surface Areas and Volumes

questions.q: The total surface area of a cube with side 5 cm is:
The volume of a cuboid with dimensions 4 cm × 3 cm × 2 cm is:
The curved surface area of a cylinder with radius 7 cm and height 10 cm (π=22/7) is:
The volume of a sphere with radius 3 cm (π=3.14) is:
The total surface area of a hemisphere with radius 5 cm (π=3.14) is:
The volume of a cone with radius 3 cm and height 4 cm (π=3.14) is:
The lateral surface area of a cube with side 6 cm is:
A cylinder has volume 1540 cm³ and height 10 cm. Its radius (π=22/7) is:
A cube and a sphere have the same volume. The ratio of their surface areas is:
questions.explanation: Volume equality: a³ = (4/3)πr³ → r = a[3/(4π)]¹/³. Surface area ratio = 6a² / 4πr² = (6a²)/(4πa²[3/(4π)]²/³) = (6/4π) × (4π/3)²/³ = (6/π)¹/³? Standard result: ratio = (6/π)¹/³

questions.q: A hollow sphere has outer radius 10 cm and inner radius 8 cm. Find the volume of material used.
A cone and a hemisphere have equal bases and equal volumes. The ratio of their heights is:
questions.explanation: Volume cone = (1/3)πr²h_c, Volume hemisphere = (2/3)πr³. Equate: (1/3)πr²h = (2/3)πr³ → h = 2r. Hemisphere has height = r, so ratio h_c : h_h = 2r : r = 2:1

questions.q: A cylindrical pipe has inner diameter 4 cm and outer diameter 6 cm. Its length is 14 cm. Find the volume of metal in the pipe.
questions.explanation: Inner r=2, outer r=3. Volume = πh(R²-r²) = (22/7)×14×(9-4) = 44×5 = 220 cm³

questions.q: How many 2 cm cubes can be cut from a 10 cm cube?
questions.explanation: Volume of big cube = 1000 cm³, volume of small cube = 8 cm³, number = 1000/8 = 125

questions.q: A sphere of radius 3 cm is melted and recast into a cylinder of radius 2 cm. Find the height of the cylinder.
questions.explanation: Volume sphere = (4/3)π×27 = 36π cm³. Volume cylinder = π×4×h = 4πh. Equate: 4πh = 36π → h = 9 cm
